blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — haloperidol decanoate labeled use
stem: Which client best matches the labeled use of haloperidol decanoate injection?

options.A: An adult with schizophrenia who is already stabilized on a consistent dose of immediate-release oral haloperidol and needs ongoing long-acting antipsychotic treatment.
options.B: An adult with acute severe agitation who needs an antipsychotic effect within minutes and has not been stabilized on immediate-release oral haloperidol.
options.C: An adult receiving haloperidol for the first time who has schizophrenia but has not previously taken a stable dosage of immediate-release oral haloperidol.
options.D: An older adult with dementia-related psychosis who needs chronic behavioral control despite the boxed warning for increased mortality in that population.

rationale: Current haloperidol decanoate labeling states that the injection is indicated for treatment of schizophrenia in adults who were previously taking a stable dosage of an immediate-release oral haloperidol product. It is administered by deep intramuscular injection every 4 weeks by a healthcare provider. Therefore A best matches the labeled use. B describes an acute rapid-treatment need rather than the long-acting indication, C lacks prior stabilization on immediate-release oral haloperidol, and D describes dementia-related psychosis, for which haloperidol decanoate is not approved and carries a boxed mortality warning.
educational_objective: Identify haloperidol decanoate as a long-acting intramuscular formulation labeled for adults with schizophrenia who were previously stabilized on immediate-release oral haloperidol.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as plausible client profiles without the original absolute-word distractor cue.
Length-balanced the choices and preserved one profile that uniquely satisfies the current labeled indication and prior-stabilization requirement.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current labeled indication. B is an acute-treatment scenario, C lacks prior oral stabilization, and D conflicts with the dementia-related-psychosis boxed warning and nonapproval.
